prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Edit target: attached ORIGINAL 16x28 green tree sprite. Create a fresh pixel-art remaster directly from this original. Final game asset must be 32 pixels wide by 56 pixels high, portrait aspect 4:7.
Design everything on a strict coarse 32x56 logical pixel grid shown enlarged. Every visible contour and shading step is a whole logical pixel. The goal is simple, chunky old-school pixel art, not fine detailed foliage.
Keep the original identity and proportions: a compact pointed teardrop-shaped evergreen, full rounded lower crown, dense cohesive green canopy, a few subtly scalloped branch tiers, and a very short tiny brown trunk at bottom center. Preserve the cool emerald/jade/teal-green palette. The crown should look like one continuous tree with only 4 broad foliage tiers, a pointed top, slightly irregular stair-step outline and restrained upper-left lighting. No long spiky outward branches.
Use roughly 8 solid coherent colors total. Shade with a few large, hand-placed irregular green clusters, about 3-5 logical pixels across, and broad deep-green right-side/underside shadow masses. A few grouped pale-green leaf tips, no bright mint streaks. Make the tree readable and naturally imperfect at its actual tiny 32x56 size. Keep the large simple shapes of the source and add only modest structure at twice its original pixel resolution.
Remove needle-by-needle detail, tiny specks, dithering, microtexture, detailed bark, glossy highlights and thin branch tracery. No blur, antialiasing, smooth gradients, painterly foliage, photography, vector or 3D appearance.
Single complete tree centered and nearly filling a 4:7 canvas, only a thin transparent margin, tree tip and trunk fully inside the frame. Genuine transparent alpha background, no cast shadow, ground, grass, scenery, objects, text, watermark or border.
